question: Why the original's long strategic redeployments keep to the railways where OpenHOI3 took a shorter road over poor land.

addresses.name: CArmy::MayStandIn
addresses.comment: **CArmy slot 34.** A sea province only where a fleet of the same owner is there that is in no battle, not moving, not retreating and can still carry the unit's weight (0x5CEFB0). A land province only where its owner area's slot 0 (province +0x2B4) says yes - which is **whether the province is in an owner area at all**: COwnerArea's slot 0 is ReturnTrue and CNullOwnerArea's ReturnFalse (FINDINGS-aihelpers.md). A province is in an area when somebody holds it and it has more than one level of infrastructure built, so **no land unit stands in, or a route passes through, land with one level of infrastructure or none**; seen in the running game 2026-11-10, a very safe search from 47 to 658 never adding a neighbour of one level and adding every one of two or more (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 32). That, and no step cost, is why a redeploying unit keeps to the railways - then yes outright where the byte at CArmy +0x1A8 is set and the province's owner is the owner of the province the unit is in, and CUnit::MayStandIn otherwise. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 32.
addresses.evidence: Each province CPathFind::Find added and took logged live (breakpoints at 0x5A1390 and 0x5A1503) for 89 very safe Soviet searches over 48 hours on 2026-11-10; from 47 to 658 the six neighbours never added, 73 109 58 90 61 93, each have one level of infrastructure in the save, and the sixteen added each have two or more. With the rule OpenHOI3 finds the original's road in 57 of 60 searches set beside it, the other three not placeable.

notes: Answers FINDINGS-movement.md's open item on the owner area's slot 0, and FINDINGS-redeploy.md's question 3: the route is a finder's, kept to the railways by where a land unit may stand.
